 Pelicans will start Dejounte Murray, Jeremiah Fears, Troy Murphy III, Zion Williamson and Yves Missi against the Pacers on Wednesday. 
 Murray suffered a bruised toe during the preseason, but is good to go for the Pelicans’ opener against the Pacers. He’ll start alongside Fears, Murphy, Williamson and Missi.

 Dejounte Murray (toe) will start for the Pelicans against the Pacers. 
 After suffering a bruised toe during the preseason, Murray will be playing in the Pelicans season opener against the Pacers. This comes at no surprise as he was able to practice since the injury. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (toe) has been a full participant in recent practices and will be available for Wednesday’s game against the Pacers. 
 Murray suffered a bruised toe during the preseason, which sidelined him for a few practices. However, the swelling has since gone down, allowing the veteran point guard to practice without issue. He’ll return to his usual starting point guard role, with Jeremiah Fears as the backup. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (toe) missed practice on Monday. 
 Murray has missed multiple practices and a preseason game with this toe injury, though head coach Jamahl Mosely said previously it was just precautionary. At this point, there’s no reason to think Murray will miss the season opener, and if he continues to miss preseason games, Jeremiah Fears will continue to start in his place. 
 Jeremiah Fears 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Jeremiah Fears tallied 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and two three-pointers in Thursday’s exhibition against the Heat. 
 With Dejounte Murray sitting out Thursday’s game, Fears moved into the starting lineup in Miami. The second-year guard logged 19 minutes, finishing with one more turnover (three) than assists. Playing time shouldn’t be an issue for Fears this season, but a healthy Murray lowers his fantasy ceiling considerably. At best, Fears is a late-round flier in redraft leagues. 
 Trey Murphy 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #25 
 Trey Murphy (ankle) and Dejounte Murray (hand) are out for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Murphy and Murray remain sidelined for the Pelicans’ final game of the season. Jeremiah Fears has benefited most in terms of playing time and scoring opportunities, with Jordan Hawkins’ playing time also increasing off the bench. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (hand) is out for Friday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Friday’s game will be the fourth that Murray has missed due to a hand injury. Jeremiah Fears, who set a franchise rookie record with 40 points on Tuesday, will once again figure prominently in the Pelicans’ rotation. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (hand) is out for Tuesday’s matchup with the Jazz. 
 Murray will miss a third straight game, and it’s unclear if we’ll see him again before the season ends. Until Murray returns, Jeremiah Fears should see an elevated workload. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 DeJounte Murray (hand) is questionable to play on Tuesday against the Jazz. 
 Murray missed the Pelicans’ two most recent games, but has the possibility of taking the floor on Tuesday. The Pelicans have lost eight consecutive games and own one of the worst records in the league. Should Murray return, he’ll provide efficient scoring and solid work as both a passer and rebounder. 
 Jeremiah Fears 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Jeremiah Fears finished Sunday’s loss to the Magic with 19 points (4-of-14 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers. 
 Fears did not have a good night shooting the basketball, finishing 2-of-7 from both inside and outside of the three-point arc. But the rookie did record a complete stat line, and the turnover count of three could have been much worse. Dejounte Murray (hand) being out the last two games has freed up additional opportunities for Fears, which the Pelicans hope will pay dividends down the line. New Orleans plays three games in Week 24, and Fears should continue to log heavy minutes. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (hand) is out for Sunday’s game against the Magic. 
 Murray will miss a second consecutive game as he deals with a left hand contusion. Jeremiah Fears was the replacement in the starting lineup the last time New Orleans did not have Murray or Trey Murphy, so he’s likely to receive the nod against the Magic.

 No surprise here as Curry was listed as probable with an ankle injury. The 38-year-old point guard appeared to suffer the injury during Sunday’s open practice. Curry’s now officially good to go for the season opener against the Lakers.

 Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings. 
 Dunn is good to go after missing most of the preseason with a minor injury, and he’ll start alongside Garland in the backcourt. Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said on Saturday that Jackson would start at center, so his inclusion is unsurprising. Garland and Hachimura should lead the starters offensively.

 According to Lakers head coach JJ Redick, Cameron Carr (oblique) is “ramping up” and is day-to-day moving forward. 
 Carr, who played well during Summer League, was ruled out for Wednesday’s opener with a strained oblique. The good news is that a return to action may not be far away, with the rookie now considered day-to-day, according to Redick. Carr should slide into the back end of the Lakers’ perimeter rotation once cleared to play.

 Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, Cooper Flagg, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Wednesday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Christie and Flagg were the only starters to take on that role in the Mavericks’ final game of the 2025-26 season. Irving, Washington, and Gafford are back from injury and will round out the starting five on Opening Night. It’s unclear whether Irving’s minutes will be limited, but don’t be surprised if the Mavericks don’t ask him to take on a full workload immediately.
